observation_summary: The optimizer accepts boundary ranges that are too large, causing subsequent normalization calculations to produce NaN. This leads to an unexpected MathIllegalStateException instead of the expected NumberIsTooLargeException.
hypothesis: The CMAESOptimizer fails to validate that the range between lower and upper bounds is finite and representable. When the range exceeds Double.MAX_VALUE, the normalization/denormalization logic (specifically in encode/decode) produces NaN values. The optimizer should detect this invalid configuration during the parameter check phase and throw a NumberIsTooLargeException, but it currently proceeds to evaluate the fitness function with NaN parameters, leading to an incorrect exception.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a check in the parameter validation logic (likely in checkParameters or a similar initialization method) to ensure that the difference between upper and lower bounds does not result in an overflow or NaN during normalization.
